differentiation.title: Editing with a reason
differentiation.activity: In a 150-word paragraph containing six marked issues, identify sentence fragments, run-ons, agreement problems, and punctuation choices. Revise and explain each correction.
scaffolds: Provide a mini-lesson and a color-coded error guide
differentiation.success: At least five accurate corrections with a meaning-based explanation for three.

differentiation.title: Two edits, two effects

differentiation.title: Professional copyedit simulation

questions.prompt: Which revision most clearly corrects the misplaced modifier in “After reviewing the evidence, the conclusion seemed weak”?
questions.rationale: The person reviewing evidence must be the grammatical subject of the introductory phrase.
options: After reviewing the evidence, the weak conclusion appeared.
After reviewing the evidence, the researchers found the conclusion weak.
The conclusion, after reviewing the evidence, seemed weak.
The conclusion seemed weak, reviewing the evidence.

questions.prompt: Compare “The study was completed. Its findings were disputed.” with “Although the study was completed, its findings were disputed.” Explain how syntax changes the relationship between ideas.
questions.answer: A strong response identifies the subordinate clause and explains that the revision foregrounds the contrast between completion and dispute.
questions.rationale: Credit explanation of meaning and emphasis, not merely naming a complex sentence.

questions.prompt: Edit a 200–300-word argument for grammar, usage, and mechanics; include an editorial memo explaining five decisions and one purposeful choice you retained.
questions.answer: A corrected, readable draft and a memo distinguishing convention errors from stylistic choices.
questions.rationale: Score accuracy, preservation of meaning, and audience-specific justification.

evidence: Edited draft with conventions applied consistently
Annotated comparisons showing how punctuation or syntax changes meaning
Editorial memo justifying corrections and retained stylistic choices
instruction: Teach conventions in the context of authentic writing, not isolated worksheets alone.
Use read-aloud and sentence-combining to make grammatical effects audible.
Compare formal edited prose with purposeful speech and dialect without treating language variety as deficiency.
Separate correction for correctness from revision for rhetorical effect.
watchFor: Correcting purposeful voice without considering context
Confusing grammatical terminology with editing competence
Introducing errors while attempting concision
Focusing on minor mechanics while overlooking sentence clarity

questions.prompt: A viral post quotes a study but gives no link. What is the strongest next step?
